title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook (2026)
author: Elena Rodriguez
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's people operations practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager best practices. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and engineering managers. The document describes standard workflows, role responsibilities, timelines, templates and escalation paths to ensure a consistent, equitable, and high-velocity people experience.

Scope and principles

- Scope: Full-time engineering and product hires (IC and manager tracks), contractor intake, and internal transitions. Excludes executive compensation (handled by People Ops leadership) and legal-specific immigration processes (handled by Legal).
- Principles:
  - Candidate experience first: clear timelines, prompt communication, and constructive feedback.
  - Inclusive hiring: structured interviews, diverse slates, and scored rubrics to reduce bias.
  - Manager accountability: hiring and onboarding are manager-owned with people-ops partnership.
  - Data-driven ops: track time-to-fill, offer acceptance, onboarding completion, and calibration outcomes.

Hiring process (end-to-end)

1) Requisition and intake (owner: hiring manager + people-ops)
   - Manager opens a req in Workday with job description, expected salary band, remote/location, and urgency.
   - People Ops validates band and headcount and assigns a recruiter.
   - Target: recruiter outreach within 48 hours of req approval.

2) Sourcing and screening (owner: recruiter)
   - Sourcing channels: internal referrals, LinkedIn, GitHub, university programs, agency partners (if approved).
   - Initial screen (30 min) by recruiter to confirm basic skills, eligibility, compensation expectations, and interest.
   - Screen outcome options: Proceed to technical loop / Reject / Hold.

3) Interview loop design (owner: hiring manager)
   - Standard loop for ICs: Recruiter screen -> Technical screen (45-60m) -> Take-home or paired exercise (optional) -> Onsite loop (3-4 interviews, 45-60m each) -> Final calibration debrief.
   - Manager should build interview team with diverse representation and assign clear rubrics per interviewer.
   - Interviewers must complete the interviewer training module and sign the interviewer code of conduct.

4) Scorecards and decisioning (owner: hiring manager + recruiter)
   - Use the standardized scorecard: competencies, communication, role fit, ownership examples, and growth potential. Each competency scored 1-5 with comments required for scores <=2 or >=4.
   - Decision options: Strong Hire / Hire / Weak Hire / No Hire. A majority of Hire or Strong Hire from technical+manager leads required to extend offer.

5) Offer and negotiation (owner: recruiter + hiring manager)
   - Recruiter prepares offer packet (base salary, equity grant, title, start date, sign-on if applicable) after compensation approval.
   - Escalation: if candidate requests exceed band, recruiter escalates to People Ops Director for approval.
   - Standard offer timeline: extend verbal offer same day as decision when possible, followed by written offer within 24 hours.

6) Background checks and closing (owner: recruiter)
   - Background checks initiated upon acceptance. Start of onboarding tasks triggered when background checks are cleared or conditional start approved.

Hiring SLAs and metrics

- Time-to-fill (target): 35 calendar days median for engineering ICs.
- Recruiter first outreach: <= 48 hours after req approval.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 70% for prioritized roles.
- Interview-to-offer ratio monitoring monthly by People Ops.

Interview and assessment standards

- Structured interviews: all interviews must use the role-specific rubric and include at least one question testing for problem decomposition and one on system design (for senior roles).
- Take-home assignments: kept to <= 5 hours, clearly scoped, and evaluated with a shared rubric.
- Feedback window: interview feedback must be submitted within 24 hours of interview. Late feedback blocks decisions.

Onboarding: first 90 days (manager-owned with people-ops support)

High-level timeline

- Pre-day 1 (owner: recruiter + people-ops + manager)
  - Send welcome packet, hardware and software request to infra, calendar invites for orientation, and first-week schedule.
  - Set up Slack, email, ID badge, and tooling access (Jira, Confluence, internal repos).
  - Manager prepares 30/60/90 goals and a buddy assignment.

- Day 1-7 (owner: manager + buddy)
  - Day 1 orientation: People Ops 90-min orientation session covering benefits, payroll, workplace policies, and communications channels.
  - Team onboarding: manager-led team intro, codebase orientation, and first small onboarding task.
  - Buddy check-ins daily for first week.

- Week 2-4
  - Technical ramp: setup dev environment, walkthrough core systems, read key docs (README, architecture overview).
  - Deliverable: complete a small-ticket production bug or implement a simple feature with reviewer feedback.

- Month 2-3
  - Autonomy ramp: take on a standard-scope ticket and lead a design doc with manager review.
  - Goal: contribute measurable output (PRs merged, incidents participated) and finalize 30/60/90 goals.
  - Formal 30-, 60-, and 90-day check-ins with manager (15-30m) and people-ops checkpoint at 90 days.

Onboarding checklists (abridged)

- Manager checklist (pre-day 1):
  - Confirm laptop and accounts provisioned.
  - Invite to team channels and calendar recurring 1:1.
  - Share 30/60/90 goals and learning plan.
  - Assign buddy and schedule intro meetings.

- New hire checklist (first week):
  - Complete benefits enrollment and payroll forms.
  - Access repo and run local dev stack.
  - Complete security and compliance training modules.

Performance and feedback cycles

- Overview: Redwood runs a biannual formal performance cycle (mid-year and year-end) with quarterly informal check-ins and continuous feedback. Managers are responsible for timely reviews and calibration participation.

- Goals and OKRs:
  - Individual goals aligned to team OKRs and product goals. Goals should be SMART and include measurable success criteria.
  - Rolling goals update: managers and ICs should review goals quarterly.

- Quarterly check-ins (owner: manager)
  - Short documented conversation focusing on progress, blockers, career development and wellbeing. Use the Check-in template in Confluence.

- Formal review cadence (owner: manager + people-ops)
  - Mid-year review: calibration exercise focusing on progress toward annual goals, stretch outcomes and initial calibration.
  - Year-end review: assesses contributions against role expectations, impact, and promotion readiness.
  - Calibration: cross-team calibration meetings facilitated by People Ops to ensure equity and consistency.

- Competency framework and rating guidance:
  - Use the competency matrix for role-level expectations (technical delivery, ownership, collaboration, mentorship). Ratings are: Exceeds Expectations / Meets Expectations / Needs Improvement.
  - Required evidence: at least two examples of impact for Meets/Exceeds; for Needs Improvement provide a PIP plan and timeline.

Promotions, role changes and compensation reviews

- Promotion timeline: manager submits promotion packet (candidate summary, evidence against rubric, peer feedback) to People Ops. People Ops facilitates a promotion panel review.
- Compensation cycles: annual cycle led by People Ops; ad-hoc adjustments for market moves require manager proposal and HR approval.

Performance improvement and appeals

- Performance Improvement Plan (PIP): used as a structured plan for employees rated Needs Improvement. PIP includes objectives, success criteria, timeline (typically 60-90 days), and weekly manager check-ins. People Ops reviews all PIP decisions.
- Appeals: employees can appeal a review by submitting a written appeal to People Ops within 10 business days; People Ops will conduct an independent review involving calibration notes and interviewers as needed.

Manager playbook: day-to-day practices

- 1:1 cadence: weekly 1:1s recommended for new managers/hires; bi-weekly acceptable for tenured teams. Put 1:1 notes in the private manager doc and share action items.
- Career conversations: dedicate at least one 1:1 per quarter to career planning. Use the Career Ladder and Development Plan templates.
- Delegation and hiring: ensure managers write clear role intents and interview rubrics. Managers should proactively source internal referrals.
- Coaching and feedback best practices: be specific, timely, and balanced; focus on behavior and impact, not intent. Use the feedback sandwich sparingly and prefer direct, actionable guidance.

People Ops operational playbook (tools and templates)

- Tools: Workday (requisitions), Greenhouse (or company ATS) for interviews and scorecards, Confluence for documentation, Slack for communications, GSuite for docs, Okta for SSO, and the internal payroll portal.
- Templates available in Confluence: Job Description template, Interview Scorecard (JSON and human templates), Offer Letter template, 30/60/90 goal template, Check-in and Review templates.
- Reporting: People Ops publishes a monthly Hiring & Retention dashboard: time-to-fill, offer acceptance, new hire ramp, onboarding completion rate, headcount by org. Managers receive a monthly digest with role open counts and team performance metrics.

Escalations and support

- Hiring exceptions (pay, sign-on, relocation): escalate to People Ops Director with justification and market data.
- Onboarding issues (equipment delays, access problems): open ticket with IT Helpdesk and tag @people-ops in Slack; People Ops SLA: acknowledge within 4 business hours.
- Performance disputes: manager escalates to People Ops Partner; if unresolved, involve HRBP and Legal for potential terminations.

Appendix: sample interview scorecard (abridged)

| Competency | Description | Score (1-5) | Evidence required |
|------------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|
| Problem Solving | Breaks down ambiguous problems, chooses tradeoffs | 1-5 | Code examples, design doc |
| System Design | Architecture clarity, scalability tradeoffs | 1-5 | Diagram or design notes |
| Technical Depth | Relevant algorithms/data structures experience | 1-5 | Past projects, PRs |
| Collaboration | Cross-team communication and ownership | 1-5 | Examples of coordination |

Sample onboarding 30/60/90 checklist (abridged)

- 30-day: local dev environment ready, 1 merged PR, completed security training, first 1:1s established.
- 60-day: owns a standard feature, participates in on-call (if applicable), formal feedback from buddy.
- 90-day: independent contributor on projects, final onboarding survey submitted, people-ops checkpoint completed.
